title: Security and Privacy on 6G Network Edge: A Survey
domain: 6G Security / Edge Computing / Edge Caching / Edge Intelligence / Federated Learning / Blockchain / O-RAN

analysis_policy.focus: Extract double-edged sword framing, three-technique coverage, per-section lessons learned patterns
analysis_policy.depth: Full paper analysis including attack taxonomy, countermeasures, trade-off discussions

section_flow.title: Introduction
section_flow.summary: Establishes 6G edge requirements (100μs latency, 1Tbps throughput), introduces double-edged sword concept for edge computing/caching/intelligence, presents contributions and paper organization.
key_claims: Edge techniques are double-edged sword - enable defense but also become attack targets
First survey covering security/privacy of all three edge techniques together
FL and blockchain key solutions for decentralized edge security

section_flow.title: Existing Survey Papers and Motivation Behind This Research
section_flow.summary: Reviews 10 related surveys via comparison table, identifies gap - no survey covers both security concerns OF edge services AND edge-enabled countermeasures together.
key_claims: Current surveys focus on either threats OR countermeasures, not both
No prior survey covers edge computing, caching, and intelligence together

section_flow.title: Challenges and Requirements of Security and Privacy
subsections: Privacy Concerns (Eavesdropper, Data Abuse, Unreliable Participants)
section_flow.summary: Classifies security attacks (DoS, malware, poisoning) and privacy concerns (eavesdropping, data abuse, unreliable participants). Defines four requirements: generality, diversity, cooperation, cost-efficiency.

section_flow.title: Emerging Techniques to Enhance Security and Privacy on 6G Network Edge
section_flow.summary: Covers FL (applications, limitations), blockchain (applications, limitations), O-RAN (architecture, security concerns). Each technique has Applications→Limitations→Countermeasures structure.

section_flow.title: Security and Privacy in Edge Computing
section_flow.summary: Reviews edge computing for authentication, encryption, IDS with dedicated table (Table III) summarizing 12+ papers by threat type, attack target, solution.

section_flow.title: Security and Privacy in Edge Caching
section_flow.summary: Covers secure caching placement (blockchain, game theory), content storage (ABE, homomorphic encryption), content delivery (physical to transport layer). Table IV summarizes papers.

section_flow.title: Security and Privacy in Edge Intelligence
section_flow.summary: Most extensive section covering edge intelligence for anomaly detection, authentication. Addresses unreliable FL participants, blockchain countermeasures. Table V summarizes 20+ papers.

section_flow.title: Trade-off Between Security/Privacy and QoS
section_flow.summary: Discusses trade-offs in IoT/IIoT, vehicular networks, mobile networks. Table VI categorizes papers by trade-off metrics and solutions. References 6G KPIs (1Tbps, 100μs).

section_flow.title: Open Research Issues
subsections: Future Issues on Three Enabling Techniques
section_flow.summary: Organizes future issues by: (1) edge computing/caching/intelligence, (2) FL/blockchain/O-RAN, (3) convergence of all techniques.

section_flow.title: Conclusion
section_flow.summary: Summarizes coverage of security/privacy for three edge techniques with FL, blockchain, O-RAN as enablers.

rhetorical_contract.promise: Comprehensive survey of security/privacy issues and countermeasures for 6G edge networks covering computing, caching, and intelligence
rhetorical_contract.delivery_mechanism: Threats/Requirements → Enabling Techniques → Three Edge Services → Trade-offs → Future Directions
rhetorical_contract.unique_contribution: First survey treating edge services as both attack targets AND defense mechanisms (double-edged sword framing)

gap_identification: Reliable participant selection for collaborative learning
Trade-off optimization between security and 6G KPIs

style.register: Technical survey with practical threat analysis

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Frame key technologies as having dual nature - serving both as defense mechanisms AND attack targets
structure: Introduce technology with its primary purpose (e.g., privacy protection)
Immediately pivot with 'On the other hand...' to attack vectors
Establish this duality as central survey theme
Organize sections to cover both perspectives
Reference duality in lessons learned sections
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Edge computing/caching/intelligence 'not only significantly reduce response time...but also effectively protect privacy' vs 'network threats still exist'
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Creates balanced, comprehensive perspective; justifies extensive coverage; hooks reader attention

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Include a dedicated figure for each major technical section showing threats/attacks relevant to that specific domain
structure: Fig. N - Security and privacy in [edge computing/caching/intelligence] scenarios
Show network architecture specific to that domain
Annotate with relevant attack vectors and threat types
Reference figure at section opening
Use consistent visual style across all scenario figures
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Fig. 5 (edge computing), Fig. 7 (edge caching), Fig. 8 (edge intelligence) - each shows domain-specific threats
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Visual consistency; quick domain orientation; threat visualization

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Include a comprehensive table at each major section summarizing reviewed papers with consistent columns
structure: Place table early in section as reference
Columns: Literature, Scenario, Threat type, Attack target, Solution
Group rows by subsection topics when possible
Include 10-20 entries per table
Reference table entries throughout prose discussion
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Table III (edge computing, 12 entries), Table IV (edge caching, 14 entries), Table V (edge intelligence, 20+ entries)
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Comprehensive coverage proof; easy reference; systematic organization

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Conclude each major section with dedicated 'Lessons Learned and Summary' subsection distilling key insights
structure: Subsection title: 'D. Lessons Learned and Summary' (or similar)
Opening paragraph synthesizing section purpose
Bullet points (3-5) with key takeaways
Each bullet addresses specific gap or insight
Some bullets suggest future directions
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Sections III, IV, V, VI, VII all end with 'Lessons Learned' subsections
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Reinforces key messages; aids retention; provides section summary

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Organize technique coverage with consistent three-part structure showing practical use, challenges, and solutions
structure: 1) Applications in Edge Services: Use cases and benefits
2) Limitations and Countermeasures: Challenges with corresponding solutions
Apply structure consistently across all techniques
Use numbered subsections for clarity
End with lessons learned
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section IV covers FL and Blockchain each with 'Applications' and 'Limitations and Countermeasures' subsections
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Balanced coverage; practical perspective; identifies research gaps
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Medium - requires identifying both benefits and limitations

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Include a separate section analyzing trade-offs between security/privacy and other metrics with dedicated summary table
structure: State the trade-off problem (security vs QoS/latency/energy)
Reference target KPIs (6G: 1Tbps, 100μs)
Organize by scenario (IoT, vehicular, mobile)
Create summary table with columns: Scenario, Edge services, Reference, Trade-off metrics, Solution
Discuss lightweight solutions and optimization approaches
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section VIII with Table VI summarizing 15+ papers on security-QoS trade-offs
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Acknowledges practical constraints; bridges theory-practice gap; guides implementation

key_concepts.double_edged_sword: Edge techniques serve both as defense AND attack targets
key_concepts.three_edge_techniques: Edge computing, edge caching, edge intelligence
